inheritance: All canonical Japan38 discrete histories, Japan7 colour stop rule, state-aware module-function bridge v2, FDT1 calibration boundaries, and the unresolved absolute-time gate remain in force unless explicitly updated below.

field_execution_priority: JPN_36 non-destructive phyllary-state validation and reversible-access pilot
JPN_15 sticky necessity arm only after abundance/site-permission gate or in common-garden/cultivated material
JPN_06 nonsticky state/enemy-pressure validation; adhesive-addition sufficiency arm only after material-equivalence and non-target-effect validation
field_feasibility.key_reordering_reason: Scientific information value is not the same as wild-field feasibility. JPN15 is an official EN taxon in Kumamoto Red List 2024 and JPN06 has regional conservation concern; JPN36 is widespread across Honshu/Shikoku wetlands and is better suited to first non-destructive manipulation-pilot work, subject to local permission.

JPN36.habitat: lowland-to-subalpine wetlands and paddy levees in Honshu/Shikoku
JPN36.first_gate: confirm live appressed state and validate reversible access proxy without tissue removal

JPN15.conservation_signal: Kumamoto Red List 2024 EN; do not assume a wild manipulation population is ethically or administratively available
JPN15.first_gate: identify an abundant explicitly permitted population or controlled/common-garden material before the necessity manipulation
JPN15.primary_causal_arm: natural sticky state neutralization versus sham within JPN15

JPN06.habitat: dry montane grasslands in central/southern Japan
JPN06.conservation_signal: regional concern including Kyoto endangered and Hyogo B-rank/rare; grassland loss is documented
JPN06.secondary_causal_arm: adhesive/restoration sufficiency treatment only after material-equivalence and non-target-effect validation; not a first wild-field manipulation

coverage_repairs.JPN34_orientation: resolve primary state before experiment ranking
coverage_repairs.JPN15_phyllary: resolve photographically/authority-side; keep separate from JPN15 stickiness role
coverage_repairs.JPN24_stickiness: resolve natural state before experiment ranking

execution_order.first: Pilot JPN36 with observation-only state confirmation followed by a reversible non-damaging phyllary-access proxy versus sham if local permission allows.
execution_order.second: In parallel, locate/verify non-destructive JPN06 and JPN15 populations and determine abundance, access, land-manager permission, and conservation constraints without committing to manipulation.
execution_order.third: Run JPN15 sticky neutralization only where the permission/abundance gate is satisfied or using controlled/common-garden material. Keep JPN06 as ancestry-matched external context and reserve adhesive-addition as a secondary sufficiency arm.
execution_order.fourth: Repair JPN34 orientation, JPN15 phyllary, and JPN24 stickiness primary states and recompute histories before adding new transition-specific systems.
execution_order.fifth: After a focal functional contrast is experimentally established, use FDT4/FDT7 to test corresponding niche/context models; do not reverse the order by mining ecology for a preferred adaptive story.

do_not_repeat: Do not rank field systems by phylogenetic information alone while ignoring conservation and permit constraints.
Do not manipulate a red-listed wild population by default merely because it is the strongest sister contrast.
Do not use destructive phyllary removal as the first JPN36 manipulation.
Do not neutralize JPN06 or JPN36 stickiness because both are currently nonsticky/nearly-nonsticky.
Do not interpret flowering-season overlap of JPN06/JPN15 as a common-garden or sympatric natural experiment; their habitat/range contexts differ.
Do not treat regional red-list status as a species-wide legal prohibition; verify site-specific rules before field work.
claim_boundary: Field-feasibility and ethical execution contract only. Distribution, phenology and regional conservation information determine where a causal test may be feasible; they do not establish adaptation, transition direction, site occupancy in the coming season, or permission to collect/manipulate plants.
